content.text:
oh-my-openagent is a TypeScript agent harness with an unusual meta-workflow: the maintainer says every feature, fix, and issue triage is being built live with an AI assistant in Discord.

The repo was previously called oh-my-opencode, and the current framing is “omo; the best agent harness.” That is a big claim, but the direction is interesting for developers working with AI coding agents.

Why people may pay attention: the project sits in the messy middle of agent workflows. Its topics point at Claude Code, Claude skills, OpenAI/ChatGPT, Anthropic, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, orchestration, TUI, and IDE usage. In other words, it looks less like “one more chatbot” and more like glue for running and coordinating agent-based development flows.

The plain technical idea: use a TypeScript harness as the control layer around coding-agent tools and workflows. Instead of treating each agent interface as a separate silo, omo appears to be exploring the orchestration layer around them: terminal interaction, IDE-adjacent usage, and multi-agent/tooling coordination.

The most interesting part might be the process, not the code: the README says the maintainer is building it in public with Jobdori, an AI assistant running on a heavily customized fork of OpenClaw, with work happening live in Discord.

Caveat: there are no star or growth signals available here, and the “building in public” workflow is README-reported. This is early-signal, operator-flagged, not proven adoption yet.

Would you use a shared harness across coding agents, or do you prefer each agent to stay in its own tool?
